`VideoComponent` can use 2D or 3D video as the texture of a video material and map it onto the surface of a created 3D model, enabling video playback on the object's surface. `VideoComponent` is an extremely flexible component capable of adapting to any third-party video player.
## Procedure
When using `VideoComponent`, it is necessary to first create `VideoMaterial` and `MeshResource` objects, then bind them to `VideoComponent` respectively.
To associate `VideoComponent` with a third-party player, create a `SurfaceRenderTexture` object through a `VideoMaterial` instance. This object can provide a standard Android `Surface`, and the player can render video frames on this `Surface`.

### Step 1: Create a video player and set a video source
Using Android's built-in `MediaPlayer` as an example, create a `MediaPlayer` object and set a video source. Code sample:
```Kotlin
val mediaPlayer = MediaPlayer()
mediaPlayer.setDataSource("your_video_path.mp4")
mediaPlayer.prepare()
```

### Step 2: Create VideoComponent and add it to an entity
Creating `VideoComponent` requires an `Entity`, a `MeshResource`, and a `VideoMaterial`:

* `MeshResource`: Used to represent the geometric shape of a 3D object that holds video frames, such as a sphere, hemisphere, cylinder, 3D patch, and more.
* `VideoMaterial` is used to contain video image. Then, create a `SurfaceRenderTexture` object and bind it to `VideoMaterial`. Next, use `VideoMaterial` to create a `SurfaceRenderTexture` object, and call the `acquireSurface()` method on the `SurfaceRenderTexture` object to get a `Surface` object. Finally, pass the `Surface` object to the `MediaPlayer` object to implement video playback.

Code sample:
```Kotlin
val videoEntity = remember{Entity()}
val surfaceRender = remember { mutableStateOf<SurfaceRenderTexture?>(null) }
SpatialView(
    modifier = Modifier.size(782.dp, 412.dp),
    initial =  { content, _ ->
    
    // Create mesh
    val mesh = MeshResource.createPlane(0.9f, 0.45f, 0.0f)
  
    // Create VideoMaterial
    val videoMaterial = VideoMaterial(BlendingMode.OPAQUE,
        VideoDimensionMode.MONO,
        MaterialCullingMode.BACK)
    
    // Create surface and set surface to player
    surfaceRender = SurfaceRenderTexture()
    surfaceRender.toGlobal()
    if(surfaceRender?.valid)
    {
        // Bind surfaceRender to VideoMaterial
        videoMaterial.bindSurfaceRenderTexture(surfaceRender)
        //Get surface and set to player
        val surface = surfaceRender?.acquireSurface()
        surface?.apply{
            mediaPlayer.setSurface(surface)
        }
    }
    
    
    // Create VideoComponent    
    val videoComponent = VideoComponent(mesh, videoMaterial)
    
    // Create entity
    videoEntity.apply {
        components.set(videoComponent)
    }
    content.addEntity(videoEntity)
    
    // Start playing media
    mediaPlayer.start()
    }) 
```

### Step 3: Destroy an entity instance
When video playback ends and the video playback service is no longer needed, proactively call `destroy()` to destroy the `Entity` instance and reclaim resources. If you do not explicitly call `destroy()`, the SDK will automatically destroy the `Entity` instance when the app exits.
```Kotlin
onDispose {
   mediaPlayer?.stop()
   mediaPlayer?.release()
   videoEntity?.destroy()
}
```

## Advanced settings
### Set video texture sampling mode
Through the broadcasting feature of the video node (`videoTexture`), each `VideoComponent` can broadcast the video texture on it for subsequent video effects processing.
You can use the `setTextureSampleName` and `setTextureSampleMode` methods of `VideoComponent` to set the sampling name and sampling mode of the video texture respectively, enabling customized processing of the broadcasted video texture. It is important to note that the sampling name you set must be consistent with the sampling name in the user-defined `ShaderGraphMaterial`.
The `VideoTextureSampleMode` property is used to specify the sampling method of the built-in video sampling node (`videoTexture`). Different modes pre-apply different visual effects to the texture output by the video sampling node. You can select the appropriate sampling mode according to actual needs and use the output video texture in the subsequent `ShaderGraphMaterial` processing for custom effects. You can dynamically switch sampling modes during runtime or debugging to quickly compare different visual effects. The available sampling modes are as follows. 
| **Mode** | **Description** | **Use case** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NONE` | Default mode. Do not output the content of the `videoTexture` node. | If the sampling mode is not explicitly set, the system will use the `NONE` mode by default, and the content of the `videoTexture` node will not be output. This default behavior does not require additional user configuration and meets basic needs in typical use cases where displaying the content of the `videoTexture` node is not necessary. |
| `RAW` | Directly output the original content of the `videoTexture` node. | To build a mirror reflection effect, the `RAW` mode can be used to output the video texture, and then subsequent image processing algorithms can process the output of the original `videoTexture` node to achieve the desired mirror reflection effect. |
| `RAW_AND_BLURRED` | Apply Gaussian blur processing to the video texture output by the `videoTexture` node, generating a blurred image. | Suitable for simulating depth of field, softening edges, and similar use cases. For example, when rendering video frames that require a soft atmosphere or hiding details, you can use `RAW_AND_BLURRED` mode to display dreamlike scenes, or blurring the background to highlight the foreground subject. <br> When building video effects with a sense of space, you can use `RAW_AND_BLURRED` mode to further enhance depth-of-field effects and spatial depth. |
The code sample is as follows:
```Kotlin
// Create an entity to host the video content
val videoEntity = Entity()

// Calculate the width and height of the video using the temporary system scale factor
val width = 1.6f * TempSystemConverter.TEMP_SCALE
val height = 0.8f * TempSystemConverter.TEMP_SCALE

// Create a plane mesh for rendering the video content
val mesh = MeshResource.createPlane(width, height, 0.0f)

// Create and configure a Transform component to control the position and scale of the video
val trans = TransformComponent()
videoEntity.components[TransformComponent::class.java] = trans
trans.setPosition(Vector3(0F, 0.0F, 0F))
trans.setScaleVector(Vector3(1.0F))

// Load the asset bundle that contains the custom ShaderGraph
val videoBundle = remember { AssetBundle.load("asset://Video/VideoCustomEffect.bundle") }

// Load the custom ShaderGraphMaterial from the asset bundle and make it globally available
val customMaterial = remember {
    ShaderGraphMaterial.loadFromAssetBundle(
            videoBundle,
            "stereoEffectVideo/Root/Cube/StereoMaterial",
        )
        .apply { toGlobal() }
}

// Create a VideoMaterial to define the basic video rendering properties
val videoMaterial =
    VideoMaterial(
        BlendingMode.OPAQUE,
        VideoDimensionMode.SIDE_BY_SIDE,
        MaterialCullingMode.BACK,
        Color4.BLACK,
    )
    
// If the custom material is successfully loaded, set the required ShaderGraph parameters
if (customMaterial.valid) {
    customMaterial.setParameter("fov", 76.394f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("aspectRatio", width / height)
    customMaterial.setParameter("windowSize", Vector2(width, height))
    customMaterial.setParameter("immersiveProgress", 0.0f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("ipd", 0.00f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("shift", 0.00f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("scale", 0.5f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("viewPortDepth", 0.2f)
    customMaterial.setParameter("originDistance", 1.0f)
}

// Attach the custom ShaderGraphMaterial to the VideoMaterial
videoMaterial.attachShaderGraphMaterial(customMaterial)

// Create a VideoComponent that combines the mesh and the video material
val component = VideoComponent(mesh, videoMaterial)
videoEntity.components[VideoComponent::class.java] = component

// Set the video texture sampling name
component.setTextureSampleName("blurColor")

// Set the video texture sampling mode
component.setTextureSampleMode(VideoTextureSampleMode.RAW_AND_BLURRED)
```

### Set video display mode
The `DisplayMode` property is used to set the display mode of `VideoComponent` when playing 3D videos containing binocular parallax information.
This property only applies to 3D videos.

The available video display modes are as follows:
| **Mode** | **Description** | **Use case** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NONE` (default) | Initial display state of video. The video display method is determined by the `VideoDimensionMode` property of the video material. | The player automatically determines the display of video based on the 3D encapsulation format of the video itself. |
| `MONO` | Display the video as a flat image without producing a stereoscopic effect. | When playing 3D videos but stereoscopic vision is not required, stereoscopic videos can be displayed as 2D. |
| `STEREO` | Display the video in a stereoscopic view, presenting a distinct 3D effect. | For 3D videos that require a high level of visual immersion, such as movie playback, virtual cinemas, or interactive experiences. |
You can use the `setDisplayMode` function to set the display mode of `VideoComponent`:
```Kotlin
Button(
    onClick = {
        entity?.apply {
            if (selectName == R.string.mv_hevc) {
            
                // Ensure the entity has a VideoComponent attached
                if (entity.components.has(VideoComponent::class.java)) {
                
                    // Retrieve the VideoComponent
                    val videoComponent = entity.components[VideoComponent::class.java]!!
                    
                    // Switch between MONO and STEREO modes
                    if (displayMode == "MONO") {
                        videoComponent.setDisplayMode(DisplayMode.MONO)
                        displayMode = "STEREO"
                    } else {
                        videoComponent.setDisplayMode(DisplayMode.STEREO)
                        displayMode = "MONO"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    },
    size = IconButtonDefaults.iconButtonSize(200.dp, 36.dp),
    modifier =
        Modifier.width(200.dp).height(36.dp).background(color = Color.Transparent),
) {

    // Show the display mode of the current video
    Text(text = displayMode, color = Color.White, fontSize = 25.sp)
}
```

### Set video texture usage flag
In the video rendering pipeline, the usage of texture buffers may be restricted by security policies and hardware capabilities. The `TextureUsageFlag` property provides a set of bitmask flags for declaring security and hardware-specific restrictions when creating video-related `SurfaceRenderTexture` objects.
| **Flag** | **Description** | **Constraints and security implications** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TEXTURE_USAGE_NON | Default flag, indicating that the texture buffer does not have any special usage requirements and can be used in any use case without hardware protection constraints. Textures created with this flag can be freely accessed and processed by the standard rendering pipeline. | * No additional security restrictions. <br> * The texture can be accessed and processed normally by the standard rendering pipeline. |
| TEXTURE_USAGE_PROTECTED_CONTENT | Enforce that the texture buffer can only be processed in a secure hardware environment, typically used for content requiring DRM protection. Textures created with this flag have restricted access permissions and cannot be processed by non-secure software components. <br> This flag is especially suitable for DRM-protected media content that requires hardware-level security assurance. <br> ***Note***: PICO Emulator does not support this flag. | * Texture content cannot be captured or have screenshots taken by non-secure applications. <br> * Direct memory access to the texture buffer is restricted. <br> * The texture can only be used through hardware-protected rendering paths. |
The code sample is as follows:
```Kotlin
// Create a SurfaceRenderTexture with the protected content flag
val surfaceRenderTexture = videoMaterial.fetchSurfaceRenderTexture(
    width = 1920,
    height = 1080,
    usageFlag = TextureUsageFlag.TEXTURE_USAGE_PROTECTED_CONTENT
)

// Create a SurfaceRenderTexture without any special flag
val defaultTexture = videoMaterial.fetchSurfaceRenderTexture(
    width = 1920,
    height = 1080
)
```

Important notes:

* When using `TEXTURE_USAGE_PROTECTED_CONTENT`, ensure that the app has the necessary permissions to handle protected video content.
* Not all devices support protected content textures. Always check device capabilities before using protected content-related flags in production environments.
* Currently, you can only set one texture usage flag for one `SurfaceRenderTexture`.

## API reference
The `VideoComponent` class provides functions related to video data rendering. For more information, refer to the [API Reference](https://developer.picoxr.com/spatial-api/index.html).
